title: Location is Key: Leveraging LLM for Functional Bug Localization in Verilog Design
problem: Automatic Verilog bug localization methods only suggest buggy line sets rather than precise identification, and depend on expert-written verification tools.
motivation: Reducing design verification time requires precise bug localization without expert-written testbenches and reference models.
method: LiK is a specialized Verilog LLM trained from Deepseek-Coder via continuous pre-training, supervised fine-tuning on bug localization, and reinforcement learning to reduce localization errors.
key_novelty: LLM specialized for precise Verilog functional bug localization trained via continuous pre-training, SFT, and RL.
contributions: Open-source specialized Verilog bug localization LLM (LiK)
Three-step training approach: continuous pre-training, SFT, and reinforcement learning
Superior accuracy over SOTA traditional method (Strider) and closed-source LLMs
Improves LLM-based Verilog debugging tool success rate from 76.47% to 90.54%

metrics.accuracy: outperforms Strider, GPT-o1, Claude-3.5; 90.54% vs 76.47% debugging success

limitations: Applicability to non-Verilog HDL languages and complex multi-module designs not discussed.
